title: SQRT of a negative real — vendor-defined: some return NaN, some abort, some return |x| silently
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE NORM_STD_DEV(VAR, SIGMA)
C     SIGMA = SQRT(VAR). VAR is supposed to be a variance >= 0,
C     but accumulated FP error can produce tiny negatives near zero.
C     IBM XL Fortran (default): traps. GFortran: NaN. Some IRIX
C     Fortran: returns SQRT(|VAR|). Behaviour is genuinely
C     platform-dependent.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      REAL VAR, SIGMA
      SIGMA = SQRT(VAR)
      END
notes: The 'common fix' is SIGMA = SQRT(MAX(VAR, 0.0)) — a tiny defensive clamp that hides the FP-error-near-zero issue. Whether the legacy code applies it determines whether the rewrite needs the same guard. Surface as an SME open question.
